saints.name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A learned virgin-martyr of the early Church, honoured as a patroness of philosophers and students…
biography: According to her ancient and much-loved passion, Catherine was a young and highly educated Christian noblewoman of Alexandria in the early fourth century. Brought before the emperor during a persecution, she is said to have confuted the pagan philosophers summoned to refute her, converting some of them to Christ.

Condemned to die upon a spiked wheel that, tradition says, broke at her touch, she was at last beheaded; her body was later venerated at the great monastery on Mount Sinai. One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, she is invoked as a patroness of philosophers, students, and those who work with wheels.
saints.knownFor: Confounding pagan philosophers and dying for the faith.
